subject: Unitization playbook: long-prefix/heartbeat billing clarifications
messages:
From: Suman Rao <suman@tricord.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Billing for long prefixes / heartbeat semantics

Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Tricord is excited about the latency and KV cache reuse. Before we move to an SOW, procurement needs clarity on three items so we can map to our internal chargeback model: 

1) Long-prefix reuse: if we send a 30k-token patient context (ingest) and then 2k-token per-request prompts that reuse the KV cache, are we billed for the full 30k each time or is there a prefix credit? Example attached (tricord_questionnaire.xlsx).

2) Heartbeat/ping semantics: our service will keep light heartbeats (small POSTs) every 30s to maintain warm KV. Do heartbeats incur the session minimum, or are they treated as metadata with different rounding?

3) Rounding & minimums: what quantum do you round to (per-call, per-60s window, per-session)? We need a deterministic formula for our finance team.

Can you reply with examples and a short numerical playbook? If you prefer, we can do a 30-minute call Monday.

—Suman
Procurement Manager, Tricord Health
[attachment: tricord_questionnaire.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Suman Rao <suman@tricord.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2027 12:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Billing for long prefixes / heartbeat semantics

Suman — thanks for the clear asks. High level answers below, followed by a short worked example. I'm cc'ing Kim and Vanessa to make sure ops/contracting align: 

1) Long-prefix reuse: we provide a prefix (KV) credit policy. The initial ingest (your 30k) is billed once at full token units. Subsequent calls that hit the same warm KV are billed only for the delta tokens in the request plus an automatic prefix credit equal to the last successful full-prefix cost for the session window. In practice that means you will not be charged 30k repeatedly if the same KV is reused inside your session window.

2) Heartbeats: heartbeats below 64 tokens (typical small pings) are charged but aggregated into a session heartbeat bucket. We apply a heartbeat minimum of 1 unit per 60s window; if your app pings every 30s, that will effectively be 1 unit/minute.

3) Rounding & minimums: our default quantum is 10 tokens for per-request rounding and a 60-second session window for heartbeat/session minimums. For longer streaming sessions we apply a session-floor of 1 compute unit per minute, billed per-minute but rounded up to the nearest 10-token equivalent per-minute.

Worked example (illustrative):
- Day 0: Ingest 30,000 tokens (charged at 30,000 token units).
- Day 1: 2,000-token request that hits warm KV: charge = 2,000 (request tokens) + 0 (prefix credit applied) then rounded up to quantum (nearest 10) => 2,000.
- Heartbeat every 30s for 24 hours => 2 heartbeats/min => billed as 1 unit/min (heartbeat minimum) -> equivalent to 60*24 = 1440 units for the day (converted to token-equivalent at your pricing tier).

If you want exact invoice-like numbers I can drop a short calc file into Drive; attached is a draft playbook (unitization-playbook-draft.pdf). Also Kim has a proposed KV-credit formula she can share.

Would you prefer that we (a) include prefix-credit language in the SOW, or (b) keep it as an operational credit applied in Console and documented in billing appendix? We usually do (b) for speed, but will do (a) if you need contractual certainty.

Happy to jump on a call Monday (I have 10–11am PT free).

—Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: unitization-playbook-draft.pdf (pdf)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2027 08:41:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Billing for long prefixes / heartbeat semantics

Forwarding with a couple notes for the record + calc.

Key technical clarifications to lock before SOW: 
- KV credit calculation: we tie the prefix credit to the most recent full ingestion event for that customer+model variant. Credit = min(original_ingest_cost, current_session_reuse_limit). This prevents credit inflation if you re-ingest different large prefixes. See kv-credit-calc.xlsx attached for a sample walk-through.
- Edge case: if the ingest is partially evicted from cache (e.g., sequence > cache size), the credit decays linearly over a sliding 24-hour window rather than drop off immediately. We gave Tricord a one-week exception during pilot but need to document.

Pricing exception ask: Tricord is requesting a pilot discount that effectively lowers the token unit rate by 15% for the first 90 days. Per pricing policy, discounts >10% need head-of-pricing sign-off. Rishi — can you confirm if we can approve 15% for a 90-day pilot (DEAL-8742)? If not, what's the max pilot discount you will approve without escalations?

Thanks — adding internal calc: [attachment: kv-credit-calc.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

—Kim
Director, Customer Solutions

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Billing for long prefixes / heartbeat semantics

All good from contracting POV — a few requests so Legal can insert unambiguous language into the SOW: 

1) Define 'session window' formally: recommend: "session window" = contiguous set of requests from the same API key where inter-request gap <= 60s; session expires after 60s of inactivity.
2) Define 'heartbeat' and state that heartbeats aggregate into session heartbeat bucket and are subject to session-floor rounding as Sergio described.
3) Add a note on cache-eviction decay: linear decay over 24 hours as Kim noted; pilot exception should be codified with explicit start/end dates.

If you (Sergio) can update the short SOW snippet with those definitions I'll circulate a redline. Attached a suggested snippet for Legal (contract-redline-snippet.docx).

—Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
[attachment: contract-redline-snippet.docx (document)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Billing for long prefixes / heartbeat semantics

Thanks team. Approve pilot concession but with a cap: we can offer a 10% pilot discount automatically. For a 90‑day pilot at 15% we need a documented revenue forecast and approval from Finance; I'll consider 12% if the customer commits to a 6-month minimum spend at the target ARR. The rule-of-thumb: 

- <=10%: ok for AE approval
- 10–15%: requires head-of-pricing sign-off (I can approve up to 12% for 6-mo commit)
- >15%: escalate to Finance.

Sergio — proceed with the SOW language (Vanessa's definitions are good). Lock pilot as 10% unless procurement pushes. If they insist on 15% bring me their forecast and we'll take to Finance.

Also, make sure the billing appendix has the worked numerical examples Suman requested — Kim's kv-credit-calc.xlsx + Sergio's playbook should be attached in the SOW Appendix.

—Rishi Malhotra
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference
